properties.name: Nothing lands on main directly — branch, open a PR, get the gates green, then merge
properties.statement:
EVERY change reaches main through a branch and a pull request. The PR is what makes CI run at all (`ci.yml` is `on: push` for main only, plus `on: pull_request`), the gates must be green before merge, and the branch is deleted by the merge.

ADVISORY — Anthony, 2026-08-09, answering the consequence question as the governance-proposal skill puts it ("if somebody pushed straight to main with a good change and passing tests, should the build have stopped them?"): advice, record it, do not gate.

WHY ADVISORY IS THE HONEST ANSWER HERE AND NOT A HEDGE. This project's governance is one developer with occasional feedback from one other person (Anthony, 2026-08-09: "the management/governance is just me, a single developer with occasional feedback from my brother Alex on it"). There is nobody to stop. A gate on this rule would be the sole author gating himself, which buys no protection and costs a detector — and `dec:does-enforced-default-to-gate-blocking` exists precisely to stop a convention recorded in passing from asserting it could fail somebody's build.

WHAT A DETECTOR WOULD LOOK LIKE, recorded so the option stays open rather than being forgotten: assert every commit on main is a squash-merge from a pull request. Feasible, and it becomes worth writing the day a second person can push here.

WHY IT IS RECORDED AT ALL, WHICH IS THE POINT. Until 2026-08-09 this rule existed NOWHERE in the design — `dec:export-once-per-pr` was recorded, `req:pr-is-a-delta` was recorded, and the rule they both presuppose was not. It lived in an agent's memory file and in Anthony's head, and it was followed twice that day (#132, #133) by a session reading it from neither. That is `req:a-rule-knows-where-else-it-is-written-down` firing on this repository: no authoritative copy, only restatements.

THE TRAPS THAT TRAVEL WITH IT, because they cost real time and are not derivable from the rule: (1) a feature branch gets NO CI until a PR exists, so open the PR as a DRAFT to start CI and mark it ready only on green; (2) merging deletes the branch, and pushing that name again recreates it with no PR and no CI; (3) a rebased commit can carry a green that belongs to a DIFFERENT commit — verify the check run's head SHA against the PR head (`fact:defect-a-rebased-commit-keeps-a-green-that-belongs-to-another-commit`); (4) a STACKED PR merges into its base branch, not main, and if that base was already squash-merged the content is stranded while GitHub still reports MERGED.
